Privacy Policy

InterceptPilot is built for local development and QA workflows. By default, technical processing happens in the user's browser and starts only when the user explicitly activates capture for a selected tab. Optional AI Bridge workflows can share permission-controlled data with a local process on the user's device.

Local-first browser tooling

Designed to inspect and simulate network behavior without an InterceptPilot backend.

InterceptPilot is a Manifest V3 Chrome and Edge extension for frontend developers and QA teams. It helps inspect HTTP and HTTPS requests, create mock rules, review logs, and test API scenarios directly in the browser, with optional user-controlled local AI Bridge integration.

Overview

This policy explains how InterceptPilot handles technical data while supporting local debugging, request inspection, mocking, QA testing, and optional AI Bridge workflows on the user's device.

InterceptPilot does not operate a backend service, does not send captured data to external servers, and does not share or sell user data. AI Bridge, when enabled by the user, communicates with a local process configured by the user.

Single purpose

InterceptPilot has one purpose: help frontend developers and QA teams inspect browser requests, simulate API behavior, and test application scenarios locally.

Capture begins only after the user explicitly starts it, and only for the browser tab the user selects.

Data handled locally

To perform its development and QA purpose, InterceptPilot may process technical data locally such as:

  • browsing and request activity related to the user-selected tab
  • request URLs, HTTP methods, status codes, headers, and timings
  • additional technical request or response details, such as payload content, when needed for inspection, debugging, and mock flows
  • logs, rules, collections, filters, and extension settings

By default, this processing happens inside the browser on the user's device. If the user enables AI Bridge, selected and permission-controlled data may be shared with a local process on the same device, such as an MCP adapter or daemon.

AI Bridge / MCP

InterceptPilot may offer an optional AI Bridge integration that connects the extension to local tools compatible with MCP. AI Bridge stays off until the user starts it.

When enabled, the extension can communicate through a local connection such as 127.0.0.1 with a user-authorized local process, including an MCP daemon or adapter. That connection can let AI tools inspect sanitized context, requests, logs, rules, collections, and run assisted actions according to the permissions selected by the user.

Sensitive data is limited and sanitized by default. Some permissions may allow more data to be sent to the local bridge, and sensitive actions may require visual confirmation in the extension. The user can stop the connection and regenerate the connection key.

Data we do not collect

InterceptPilot does not collect or transmit data to a company backend because it has no backend.

  • no analytics or telemetry
  • no advertising identifiers
  • no cross-site tracking
  • no profiling
  • no sale of data

How data is used

Technical data is used locally and only to support the extension's visible features, including:

  • displaying inspected network activity for the selected tab in the extension UI
  • supporting local debugging, diagnostics, and QA workflows
  • creating, applying, and reviewing mock rules and collections
  • preserving settings and working context required for the tool between sessions
  • supporting optional AI Bridge workflows that the user enables and configures

Local storage

Rules, collections, filters, logs, and settings are stored in the browser's local storage area used by the extension.

InterceptPilot uses that local storage so the user can keep configurations and continue working between sessions without relying on remote infrastructure.

Third-party sharing and AI tools

InterceptPilot does not share captured data, rules, logs, or settings with third parties. It does not sell data and does not make captured technical data available to advertisers, data brokers, or external analytics providers.

InterceptPilot does not control the privacy practices of external AI tools connected by the user. If the user connects AI Bridge to an AI client or another compatible tool, that tool may process or transmit data according to its own configuration and privacy policy. Users should review the settings and policies of the AI tool they choose. InterceptPilot provides the local bridge and permission controls; it does not operate the AI provider.

Remote code

InterceptPilot does not execute remote code. Its JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and related assets are packaged with the extension itself.

The extension's scripts are loaded from extension resources, not from remote servers, and the product is not designed around externally hosted executable code.

Permissions

InterceptPilot uses browser permissions only to provide its development and QA features, such as attaching to a user-selected tab, inspecting requests, supporting debugging workflows, storing local rules and settings, rendering the extension UI, and supporting optional AI Bridge workflows when the user enables them.

These permissions are used only for the extension's stated purpose. They are not used for tracking, advertising, analytics, or background collection.

debugger activeTab tabs webNavigation scripting sidePanel storage management host permissions

User control

The user chooses when capture starts, which tab is involved, and when capture stops. InterceptPilot does not silently activate request capture across unrelated tabs.

The user remains in direct control of browser-stored rules, collections, logs, filters, and settings. When AI Bridge is enabled, the user also controls data/action permissions, can stop the local connection, and can regenerate the connection key.
